expectations.text: States that a written agreement or reminder is not enforcement
expectations.evidence: "they're all the same device: **training**. Training degrades. Half compliance after two weeks... A fourth reminder gets you the same number"

expectations.text: Recommends a pre-commit hook to run the formatter automatically
expectations.evidence: "A pre-commit hook that formats **changed files only**"

expectations.text: Notes that pre-commit is bypassable with --no-verify and must be backed by a CI check
expectations.evidence: "keep it under ~5 seconds or people will `--no-verify` it" and "The same command as a **required CI check**. This is the one that actually holds"

expectations.text: Recommends a type check as a required CI check
expectations.evidence: "branch protection with these as required checks" (referring to both formatter and type enforcement from context)

expectations.text: Recommends baselining or ratcheting rather than enforcing across the whole repo at once
expectations.evidence: "Either check changed files only, or generate a baseline of existing violations and fail only on new ones"

expectations.text: Notes that branch protection is what makes a CI check actually required
expectations.evidence: "**The piece that makes all of it real:** branch protection with these as required checks. Without it you've built a suggestion with extra steps"

expectations.text: Recommends the failure message tell the developer how to fix it
expectations.evidence: "`error: 3 files unformatted — run 'make fmt'` teaches; `rule violated` produces a workaround"

expectations.text: Does not primarily recommend rewriting CONTRIBUTING.md, more reminders, or more discipline
expectations.evidence: "**One thing to delete:** the CONTRIBUTING.md paragraph. Replace it with the command that fixes a failure"
